mainTopic: End of פרק ואלו קשרים (preparing food on יום כיפורים for after the fast) and the start of פרק כל כתבי: saving holy writings from a fire on שבת, and the מחלוקת between רב הונא and רב חסדא about holy writings in other languages.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous topic: food preparation on יום כיפורים for after the fast. Light preparation such as trimming vegetables or cracking nuts is allowed only from מנחה onward, because of עגמת נפש, and רבה stopped his household from starting earlier. After the הדרן, a new פרק begins with a משנה: on שבת we may save all כתבי הקודש from a fire, whether they are read publicly or not, and books in other languages require גניזה. The גמרא brings a מחלוקת. For holy writings in תרגום or another language, רב הונא says we do not save them, and רב חסדא says we do, to prevent בזיון. The משנה is first brought as a refutation of רב הונא, but each אמורא reads it his own way. Two ברייתות are then raised against רב הונא. He answers that this is a dispute among תנאים, and that רבי יוסי agrees with him. רבי יוסי supports his view with a story about a translated ספר איוב that was buried. רבי rejects one version of that story, teaching that holy writings may not be destroyed by hand but are left to decay on their own. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to ask which תנאים are in dispute, a question answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Trimming vegetables is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ruling begun on the previous עמוד about יום כיפורים that falls on שבת: from מנחה onward, trimming vegetables is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Trimming vegetables is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a ruling from the previous עמוד. When יום כיפורים falls on שבת, trimming vegetables is permitted from מנחה (late afternoon) onward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trimming leaves off vegetables is not a real מלאכה. It is allowed in the afternoon so food can be ready right after the fast.

keyTerms.meaning: trimming or cleaning vegetables (removing the outer leaves)

phrases.english: is permitted in trimming vegetables.
phrases.notes: The beginning of this ruling, about יום כיפורים that falls on שבת, is on the previous עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום כיפורים that falls on שבת, trimming vegetables is permitted from מנחה onward.

steps.title: Cracking nuts and seeding pomegranates on a weekday יום כיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that when יום כיפורים falls on a weekday, one may crack nuts and remove pomegranate seeds from מנחה time onward, because of עגמת נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: when יום כיפורים falls on a weekday, one may crack nuts and seed pomegranates from the afternoon onward, because of the distress of the hungry person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second, similar ruling. On a weekday יום כיפורים, a person may prepare nuts and pomegranates in the late afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is עגמת נפש. A fasting person who doesn't know food is ready suffers more in the last hours. This preparation involves no real מלאכה, so it is allowed once the afternoon arrives.

keyTerms.meaning: from the time of מנחה (late afternoon) onward

phrases.english: (And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Yom Kippur that falls on a weekday)
one may crack nuts
and remove the seeds of pomegranates
from the afternoon onward
because of distress.
phrases.notes: So that the faster knows food is ready for after the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling for a weekday יום כיפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a weekday יום כיפורים, light food preparation is allowed from מנחה onward because of עגמת נפש.

steps.title: What the households of רב יהודה and רבה did
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports the practice: רב יהודה's household trimmed cabbage, and רבה's household scraped gourds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The household of רב יהודה would trim cabbage. The household of רבה would scrape gourds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how two great households practiced this rule. It is setting up the next step, where רבה reacts to what his household did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are real-life examples of the permitted preparation for after the fast. The story shows the rule was actually practiced, and it sets the stage for a limit on it.

phrases.english: The household of Rav Yehuda would trim cabbage.
The household of Rabba would scrape gourds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling of step 2 being practiced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Great households prepared vegetables on יום כיפורים for after the fast.

steps.title: רבה stops his household from preparing too early
steps.stepSummary: When רבה saw his household preparing too early, he told them a letter had come from ארץ ישראל in the name of רבי יוחנן saying it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה saw that they were doing it early, he said to them: a letter came from the West (ארץ ישראל) in the name of רבי יוחנן that it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה noticed his household was preparing food before the proper time. He stopped them by quoting a letter from ארץ ישראל in רבי יוחנן's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency is limited. It only applies from מנחה onward, when the עגמת נפש is real. Starting earlier is forbidden, since the only reason for allowing it at all is that late-day distress.
steps.whatToRemember: Preparing food on יום כיפורים for after the fast is allowed only late in the day (from מנחה) because of עגמת נפש. Doing it earlier is forbidden.

phrases.english: Once he saw that they were doing it early,
he said to them:
A letter came from the West
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, that it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the practice in step 3 by timing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The leniency applies only from מנחה onward. Preparing earlier is prohibited.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter ואלו קשרים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק ואלו קשרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter ואלו קשרים.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter ואלו קשרים. A new chapter starts right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell to a finished chapter. It contains no legal content.

keyTerms.meaning: 'we will return to you', the formula for finishing a chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'And These Knots'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter.

steps.title: משנה: saving all holy writings from a fire on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on שבת we may save all כתבי הקודש from a fire. This applies whether or not they are read publicly, and even if they are written in any language. They also require גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: All holy writings may be saved from a fire, whether they are read publicly or not. Even if they are written in any language, they require burial.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about rescuing holy books from a fire on שבת. It says all holy books may be saved, even ones not read publicly. Books in other languages require burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one may not carry items out of a fire on שבת, but holy books are special. 'Read' means נביאים (read as the הפטרה) and 'not read' means כתובים. The phrase about other languages becomes the focus of the coming argument.
steps.confusionAlert: It is unclear in the משנה whether 'in any language' connects to 'we rescue them' or only to 'they require burial'. This exact question is what the גמרא will argue about.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: All holy writings
we rescue them from the fire,
whether they read from them,
phrases.notes: Read publicly, such as נביאים for the הפטרה.

phrases.english: or whether they do not read from them.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּתוּבִים בְּכׇל לָשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: Even though they are written in any language,
they require burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All כתבי הקודש may be saved from a fire on שבת, and those in other languages require גניזה.

steps.title: משנה: why some holy books are not read on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that כתובים are not read on שבת because doing so would take people away from the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they not read them? Because of the neglect of the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks and answers its own question: why are some holy books (כתובים) not read? The answer is that reading them would pull people away from the שבת lecture in the study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not reading them is not a sign of lower holiness. It is a practical rule to protect the public learning on שבת, so they are still holy and are saved.

keyTerms.meaning: neglect of (or taking time away from) the study hall

phrases.english: And why do they not read from them?
Because of the neglect of the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase 'not read' from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כתובים are not read on שבת because of ביטול בית המדרש, not because they are less holy.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב חסדא argue about translated holy writings
steps.stepSummary: If holy writings are written in תרגום or another language, רב הונא says we do not save them from a fire, and רב חסדא says we do.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if they were written in Aramaic translation or in any language, רב הונא said we do not save them from a fire, and רב חסדא said we do save them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a מחלוקת between two אמוראים about holy books written in a language other than Hebrew. רב הונא says they are not saved, and רב חסדא says they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether translated holy books have enough status to justify rescuing them on שבת. The next steps will explain each side.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ כְּתוּבִים תַּרְגּוּם אוֹ בְּכׇל לָשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: If they were written in translation or in any language,
Rav Huna said:
We do not rescue them from the fire,
and Rav Ḥisda said:
We rescue them from the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ אִיתְּמַר הָיוּ כְּתוּבִים תַּרְגּוּם אוֹ בְּכׇל לָשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a dispute about the משנה's phrase 'in any language'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא says translated holy writings are not saved on שבת. רב חסדא says they are.

steps.title: Defining where the argument really is
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that translations may be read, everyone agrees they are saved. The argument is only according to the view that they may not be read.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says they may be read, everyone agrees we save them. Where they argue is according to the one who says they may not be read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument. It explains that רב הונא and רב חסדא only disagree within one opinion, the one that says translated holy books may not be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an earlier dispute (בין תנאים) about whether translated holy books are fit for reading. If they are fit, nobody would let them burn. The real question is whether books unfit for reading still deserve rescue.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who says
they were given to be read (fit for reading)

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר נִיתְּנוּ לִקְרוֹת בָּהֶן —
phrases.english: According to the one who says they may be read,
everyone agrees that we rescue them.
Where they argue

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לִקְרוֹת בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: is according to the one who says they may not be read.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר נִיתְּנוּ לִקְרוֹת בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the מחלוקת in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת exists only according to the view that translations are not fit for reading.

steps.title: The reasons of רב הונא and רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says we do not save them because they are not fit for reading. רב חסדא says we save them to avoid disgrace to holy writings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: we do not save them, since they may not be read. רב חסדא said: we save them because of the disgrace to holy writings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives each אמורא's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא ties rescue to a book's use for reading: no reading, no rescue. רב חסדא says the holy content itself matters, and letting it burn would be a בזיון.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: We do not rescue them,
since they may not be read.
Rav Ḥisda said: We rescue them
because of the disgrace to holy writings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר אֵין מַצִּילִין דְּהָא לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לִקְרוֹת בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons behind the two positions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: rescue depends on fitness for reading. רב חסדא: rescue is required to prevent בזיון כתבי הקודש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the core question of the sugya. Is a holy book saved because of its use, or because of its holiness?

steps.title: Quoting the משנה against רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: all holy writings are saved, whether read or not, even if written in any language.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: all holy writings may be saved from a fire, whether they are read or not, even if they are written in any language.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the words of the משנה to use against רב הונא. This step sets up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה is quoted as one continuous sentence. That makes 'even if written in any language' sound connected to 'we rescue them', which would contradict רב הונא.

phrases.english: We learned: All holy writings
we rescue them from the fire,
whether they read from them
or whether they do not read from them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּתוּבִין בְּכׇל לָשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: even though they are written in any language.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן כׇּל כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה as a source to test רב הונא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that translated holy writings are not saved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה seems to say that books in any language are saved.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as a refutation of רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה this way: 'read' means נביאים, 'not read' means כתובים, and 'any language' means books not fit for reading. These are still saved, so this seems to be a תיובתא of רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that 'read' means נביאים, 'not read' means כתובים, and 'even in any language' means books not fit for reading? And the משנה teaches that we save them. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה phrase by phrase to show it clearly contradicts רב הונא. It ends by declaring a תיובתא, a strong refutation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each category is matched to a type of book. Then 'any language' is read as the case of books not fit for reading, which is exactly רב הונא's case. Since the משנה says to save them, רב הונא seems refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'is it not that...?', proposing a reading of a source

steps.confusionAlert: Despite the word תיובתא, this is not the end. The next passage shows רב הונא defending himself by reading the משנה differently.

phrases.english: Is it not that 'that they read from them' means the Prophets,
'and that they do not read from them' means the Writings,
'even though they are written in any language'
means those that may not be read,
and it teaches: we rescue them.
This is a refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging inference from the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that holy writings unfit for reading are not saved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה links 'any language' (books unfit for reading) with 'we rescue them'. That directly contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: רב הונא shows the challenger's reading has its own problem
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא argues that the reading of the משנה used against him does not work, because the סיפא says these books need גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can answer you: Do you really think so? Look at the end of the משנה: 'they require burial.' If we actually save them from a fire, do we even need to say they require burial?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself. He shows that reading the משנה as 'even translations are saved' runs into trouble in the very next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא of the משנה says these writings 'require גניזה' (burial). If they are important enough to save from a fire on שבת, it is obvious they need burial, so why would the משנה say it? The ending makes more sense if it is talking about books we do NOT save, which still need burial.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so? (a way of pushing back on an assumption)
The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Respectful burial or storage of holy writings

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you:
And do you really think so?
Say the latter clause: they require burial
Now, if we even save them from the fire,
is it necessary to say they need burial?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the משנה from step 12 that seemed to refute רב הונא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of the משנה that says books in any language are saved from a fire.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes the סיפא ('they require גניזה') seem obvious and unnecessary.

steps.title: רב הונא's own reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Each אמורא reads the משנה his own way. רב הונא reads it as: Hebrew books are saved, while books in other languages are not saved but still need גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא explains the משנה according to his view, and רב חסדא explains it according to his view. רב הונא explains: 'Whether they are read' means נביאים, 'or not read' means כתובים. When is this said? When they are written in Hebrew. But books in any other language are not saved, and even so, they need burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה can be read both ways. It first sets up that each side has his own reading, and then gives רב הונא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, 'any language' in the משנה is a separate case. Those books are NOT saved, but they still need גניזה. This solves the problem from step 13: the line 'they require burial' now teaches something new about books we do not save.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains the source according to his own view
When is this said? (limits a rule to a certain case)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna explains it according to his reasoning,
and Rav Chisda explains it according to his reasoning.
Rav Huna explains it according to his reasoning:
"Whether they are read" means Prophets,
"or they are not read" means Writings.
When is this said?
When they are written in the holy language (Hebrew),
but if they are in any other language, we do not save them,
and even so, they need burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the problem raised in step 13 and gives רב הונא's full reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source to fit one's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says books in any language are saved, which refutes רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Books in any language are not saved, and the סיפא teaches that they still need גניזה.

steps.title: רב חסדא's own reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reads the משנה as saving books in any language. He explains 'they require burial' as referring to the worm-eaten remains of the books.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explains according to his view: 'Whether they are read' means נביאים, 'or not read' means כתובים. Even if they are written in any language, we also save them. And this is what the משנה means: their worm-eaten remains need burial.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב חסדא gives his reading. He must explain the line about burial, since for him these books are saved anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, books in any language are saved from the fire. So 'they require גניזה' cannot mean the books themselves, because that would be obvious. Instead, it teaches that even the crumbled, worm-eaten pieces (מקק) of these books need burial.

keyTerms.meaning: Worm-eaten or crumbled remains of a book
And this is what it means

steps.confusionAlert: Both רב הונא and רב חסדא agree the books need גניזה. They disagree about whether the משנה's 'any language' books are saved from the fire, so they explain the burial line differently.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda explains it according to his reasoning:
"Whether they are read" means Prophets,
"or they are not read" means Writings,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּתוּבִין בְּכׇל לָשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: even though they are written in any language,
we also save them.
And this is what it is saying:
and their worm-eaten remains require burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the parallel reading for רב חסדא that was set up in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source to fit one's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The burial line seems unnecessary if the books are saved anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: The burial line refers to the worm-eaten remains (מקק) of the books.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה fits both views. רב הונא: books in other languages are not saved but are buried. רב חסדא: they are saved, and even their מקק is buried.

steps.title: A ברייתא says translated writings are saved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying writings in תרגום or any language are saved from a fire. This looks like a refutation of רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If they were written in תרגום or any language, we save them from the fire. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with a ברייתא that clearly says translated writings are saved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the משנה, this ברייתא has no line that can be read another way. It says outright that translated writings are saved, which goes directly against רב הונא.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If they were written in Aramaic translation or any language,
we save them from the fire.
This is a refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הָיוּ כְּתוּבִים תַּרְגּוּם וְכׇל לָשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה was settled, a new challenge is brought from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that translated writings are not saved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא states plainly that writings in תרגום or any language are saved from a fire.

steps.title: רב הונא: that תנא holds translations may be read
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that this ברייתא follows the view that translations may be read, and he already agreed those are saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can say to you: This תנא holds that they were given to be read from.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes the ברייתא aside by saying it follows the other view, which is not the view he was ruling on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 9 we learned that if translations may be read, everyone agrees they are saved. רב הונא's ruling was only for the view that they may not be read. So this ברייתא does not argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of the משנה era
They were given to be read from

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you:
This tanna holds
that they may be read from.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to the other opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the view that translations may be read, where everyone agrees they are saved.

steps.title: A ברייתא saves them even though they may not be read
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says writings in several foreign languages are saved even though they may not be read. This seems to truly refute רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If they were written in Coptic, Median, עברית (ancient Hebrew script), Elamite, or Greek, even though they may not be read, we save them from the fire. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge that blocks רב הונא's last answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says outright that these writings may not be read, and still they are saved. That is exactly the case רב הונא ruled on, so his answer from step 17 does not work here.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If they were written in Coptic, Median,
ancient Hebrew script, Elamite, or Greek,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנוּ לִקְרוֹת בָּהֶן
phrases.english: even though they may not be read from,
we save them from the fire.
This is a refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the escape route of step 17 with a source that says they may not be read.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling, even within the view that translations may not be read
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says explicitly that they may not be read, yet they are still saved.

steps.title: רב הונא: it is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that תנאים argue about this. He follows רבי יוסי, who says translated writings are not saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can say to you: It is a dispute of תנאים, as it was taught: If they were written in תרגום or any language, we save them from the fire. רבי יוסי says: we do not save them from the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא admits that some ברייתות disagree with him. He says he follows a different תנא, רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא may follow one side of a dispute among תנאים. Since רבי יוסי rules that translated writings are not saved, the ברייתא in step 18 is no longer a refutation. It simply follows the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you:
It is a dispute of tannaim,
as it was taught:
If they were written in Aramaic translation or in any language,
we save them from the fire.
Rabbi Yosei says:
we do not save them from the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by finding a תנא who agrees with רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא follows רבי יוסי, who says translated writings are not saved.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא survives the challenges because his view matches רבי יוסי's side of a dispute among תנאים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's story about the translated ספר איוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells how רבן גמליאל the elder had a translated ספר איוב buried, and his grandson did the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: There was a story with my father חלפתא, who went to רבן גמליאל the great in Tiberias. He found him sitting at the table of יוחנן הנזוף, holding a translated ספר איוב and reading from it. He said to him: I remember your grandfather רבן גמליאל standing on a step on the הר הבית. They brought him a translated ספר איוב, and he told the builder: Sink it under the row of stones. So this רבן גמליאל also ordered that it be put away, and it was buried.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי backs up his ruling with a story showing that great leaders buried translated books instead of keeping them for use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a translated book was hidden away instead of read, it shows that such books were not treated as fit for reading. That fits רבי יוסי's view that they are not saved from a fire on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: יוחנן 'the rebuked' (someone who had been reprimanded)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with my father, Chalafta,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָלַךְ אֵצֶל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּרִיבִּי לִטְבֶרְיָא,
phrases.english: who went to the great Rabban Gamliel in Tiberias,
and he found him sitting
at the table of Yochanan HaNazuf,
and in his hand was a translated book of Job,
and he was reading from it.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: The commentators disagree about who is speaking here: some say אבא חלפתא, others say יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: זָכוּר אֲנִי בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אֲבִי אָבִיךָ
phrases.english: I remember Rabban Gamliel, your father's father,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבֵּי מַעֲלָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: who was standing on top of a step on the Temple Mount,
and they brought before him a translated book of Job,
and he said to the builder:
Sink it under the row of stones.
He too gave an order about it, and it was buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאַבָּא חֲלַפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוסי's ruling quoted in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's view that translated writings are not treated as fit for reading
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבן גמליאל the elder and his grandson, who buried a translated ספר איוב

steps.title: Another version: a tub of mortar was turned over it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה tells the story differently: on the הר הבית they turned a tub of mortar over the book.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: They turned a tub of mortar over it.
steps.whatsHappening: A different תנא gives his own version of how the book was disposed of on the הר הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the book was covered with mortar, which would destroy it. This sets up רבי's objection in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
They overturned a tub of mortar on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the הר הבית story from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The translated book was covered with a tub of mortar.

steps.title: רבי rejects the mortar version with two reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבי rejects the mortar version: there was no mortar on the הר הבית, and one may not destroy holy writings with one's hands. Instead, they are left to rot on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: There are two answers to this. One: where would mortar come from on the הר הבית? And also: is it allowed to destroy them with one's hands? Rather, one puts them in a neglected place, and they rot on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives two reasons why the mortar version cannot be correct, and then explains how such books are really put away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, mortar was not used in building on the הר הבית. Second, even holy writings that are not read may not be actively destroyed. The proper way is to leave them somewhere they will decay naturally.

keyTerms.meaning: To destroy them with one's hands (actively)

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a lasting rule: holy writings, even ones not fit for reading, may not be actively destroyed. They are put away and left to decay.

phrases.english: Rebbi said:
There are two answers to this:

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא, וְכִי טִיט בְּהַר הַבַּיִת מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: One, where would mortar come from on the Temple Mount?
And further, is it permitted to destroy them with one's hands?
Rather, one places them in a neglected place,
and they rot on their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the version of the story given in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's version that mortar was poured over the book
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There was no mortar on the הר הבית, and actively destroying holy writings is forbidden.

steps.title: Who are the disputing תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask which תנאים argue on this issue according to רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא opens a new question that will be answered in the next part of the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב הונא said the question of saving translations depends on a dispute among תנאים. Now the גמרא wants to pin down exactly which תנאים hold each view.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנאים (here: the ones who disagree)

phrases.english: Who are the tannaim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב הונא's claim of a dispute among תנאים in step 19 and asks who they are.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנאים who disagree about saving translated writings according to רב הונא.
